name: NVIDIA Warp
role: Python kernel framework for particle, field and geometry simulation, CPU on macOS
notes: 2026-11-27: Triage: assess. Scriptable Python kernels bake particles, fields or meshes at a fixed step; neighbours pymunk (2D rigid), jolt-physics-js and rapier (rigid), splishsplash (SPH app).

2026-11-27: Lead said Apache-2.0 (verified: wheel metadata and LICENSE.md) and 1.19.0 uploaded 2026-11-02 (verified on PyPI). The 1.19.0 wheel has no warp.sim package, so cloth and soft bodies are not in this release; not claimed.
2026-11-27: Skill opportunity: VCR toolkit guide justified by the fixed-step fixture; macOS wheels are CPU only (no Metal).

evidence.result: CPU backend, numpy 2.5.5, Python 3.12: 64 particles with gravity, pairwise repulsion, a sphere and a floor, 600 steps at 1/60 s with 4 substeps. 9 of 9 gates pass: two process runs identical (601 hashes); 9 fresh-process re-simulations in shuffled order match the trace; no penetration; settled at 0.0117 m/s. Five atomic_add sums identical (0.746666). Agent-reviewed side view shows fall, scatter off the sphere and rest.
evidence.scope: Fixed-step CPU particle kernels, same-machine reruns and fresh-process seek; no atomics across thread counts, GPU, cloth (no warp.sim in 1.19.0), FEM or fluids, no render; macOS arm64 only.

summary: Python framework that JIT-compiles kernels (CPU, or CUDA off macOS) for particles, fields, meshes and FEM. Driven from a script, it bakes per-step arrays to numpy for a renderer or Blender. On macOS the wheel is CPU only; 1.19.0 ships no warp.sim, so no cloth or soft bodies. Distinct strength: write your own 3D simulation kernels.
use_when: Bake custom 3D particle or field simulation from Python at a fixed step
Use over pymunk when the sim is 3D or needs custom kernels
avoid_when: Use Rapier or Jolt for rigid bodies with contacts and joints
Use Pymunk for plain 2D rigid-body scenes
Avoid large simulations on macOS: CPU only, no Metal

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install warp-lang==1.19.0 numpy

assessment.rationale: Apache-2.0 per wheel metadata; 1.19.0 released 2026-11-02 with an arm64 macOS wheel (CPU only). No warp.sim in the wheel, so cloth is out of scope. A custom-kernel 3D bake route that pymunk and rapier do not cover.
